question: Where can I get the current land-use and zoning plans of the United States as geometry, with land classification and the planning instrument they belong to?

answer.summary: No single official nationwide zoning dataset was found: zoning is adopted locally. Two tested cities publish open polygon services: Denver (3,934 polygons; ordinance number/year and code version per polygon) and Austin (22,503 polygons; ordinance boundaries in a separate layer, linked only by spatial overlay). Nationwide coverage appears only as a paid commercial layer (Regrid) or a nonprofit viewer (National Zoning Atlas); neither was verified here. Zone codes are not comparable between places; future-land-use plans are separate layers.
main_caveats: Zoning is local: each city/county defines its own districts, so a code such as 'SF-3' or 'U-SU-A' only has meaning in its own code.
Only Denver and Austin were tested; thousands of other US jurisdictions were not checked and may publish nothing, a viewer or an image.
Denver mixes two codes in one layer: Denver Zoning Code (2010) and Former Chapter 59 (1956), shown by ZCODE_VERSION.
Austin links a polygon to ordinances only by overlay; one point can fall in several ordinance polygons, one being a 1999 citywide code ordinance.
Both cities state the data is informational, not for legal/engineering determinations; adopted ordinances and maps prevail.
answer.confidence_reason: Denver and Austin services were queried live; the national picture rests on two web pages (NZA, Regrid) and failed attempts to read federal and aggregator catalogues.

attributes.note: Open polygon APIs tested for Denver (3,934) and Austin (22,503); no national official geometry found; Regrid layer is paid.
attributes.gap_note: Only two jurisdictions were tested. Next step: sample other jurisdictions' GIS portals; check NZA terms and Regrid sample files. Regrid's nationwide zoning layer is sold through sales (restricted).

attributes.note: Denver ZONE_DISTRICT/ZONE_DESCRIPTION/ZONE_DIST_TYPE and Austin ZONING_ZTYPE/ZONING_BASE; codes are local and need each city's code.
attributes.gap_note: Classification vocabularies were read only for Denver and Austin; no standard national scheme was verified (Regrid sells a standardized layer, not inspected).

attributes.note: Denver: ORD_NUM/ORD_YEAR/ZCODE_VERSION per polygon. Austin: ordinance polygons with EDIMS PDF links, overlapping and incomplete before 2001.
attributes.gap_note: Denver ordinance PDFs and the Denver Municipal Code text were not opened beyond the zoning code page; Austin Land Development Code (Municode) returned 403, so code definitions were not read.

update_frequency.quote: The zoning boundaries data layer is governed by ordinance and is only changed accordingly.

attempts.note: JavaScript-rendered hub page; no frequency readable with curl.

exclusions.value: Informational data; text of PUDs, waivers and conditions is not in the layer (only PUD_NUM/PUD_DOCUMENT names and WAIVERS/CONDITIONS fields).

key_fields.meaning: District code (coded-value domain; the PUD sample shows a '1956 Zone District Domain' beside 2010 codes such as U-SU-C1)
Code generation: 2010 (Denver Zoning Code) or 1956 (Former Chapter 59)
Ordinance number and year (inferred from names; e.g. 333 / 2010)
Planned Unit Development number and document file name, e.g. 584 / 'PUD 584.pdf'

how_to_use.example_result: One feature: ZONE_DISTRICT D-CV, ZONE_DESCRIPTION 'Downtown - Civic (D-CV)', ZONE_DIST_TYPE 'Commercial Mixed Use', ORD_NUM 333, ORD_YEAR 2010, ZCODE_VERSION 2010 (queried 2026-11-20).
steps: Query layer 27 by point or envelope (inSR=4326); use f=geojson with outSR=4326 for geometry.
Read ZCODE_VERSION first, then interpret ZONE_DISTRICT with the 2010 Denver Zoning Code or Former Chapter 59.
Use ORD_NUM/ORD_YEAR to find the ordinance; open PUD_DOCUMENT names with the city for PUD text.
reading_traps: Mixed code generations in one layer: the same-looking district letters mean different things under 1956 and 2010.
ZONE_USE_FORM '999' and PUD_DOCUMENT 'NA.pdf' appeared as placeholders in the tested record.
Hosted copy edited 2024-03-12; later rezonings may be absent. Confirm with Denver before relying on it.

steps: Query by point/envelope (inSR=4326) or download pages with resultOffset (maxRecordCount 2000; 22,503 records = 12 pages).
Use f=geojson with outSR=4326 for geometry.
Interpret ZONING_ZTYPE with Austin's Land Development Code Title 25 (not read: Municode returned 403).
Overlay with the ordinance-boundaries layer to find the ordinance(s) behind the polygon.
reading_traps: Layer covers 'City of Austin and surrounding counties' but zoning only applies within city limits per the city's own notice.
Zoning By Address (Socrata) is a derived list and says it must not be used for zoning determinations.
No ordinance key in this layer; the link to an instrument is a spatial overlay.

inclusion_rule.value: Day-forward entry since 2001; older ordinances are less likely to be present. 113 rows have no CASE_NUMBER and 15 no ZONING_ORDINANCE_PATH.
inclusion_rule.quote: Work on this layer began in 2001 with zoning ordinance polygons entered on a day forward basis. Therefore, polygons for older ordinances are less likely to be included in this data.

key_fields.meaning: Link to the ordinance PDF in the City Clerk's EDIMS

how_to_use.example_result: Two ordinances: 20040513-33B (case C14-04-0012.002, type NP; PDF = rezoning to add a neighborhood plan combining district) and 19990225-070b (the 1999 ordinance replacing Title 13 with Title 25).
steps: Take the zoning polygon's location and intersect it with this layer.
Pick the ordinance whose type matches the district suffix (e.g. NP for SF-3-NP); expect a citywide code ordinance too.
Open ZONING_ORDINANCE_PATH (EDIMS PDF) and read the zoning case and exhibit.
reading_traps: Overlapping polygons: one point returned a citywide 1999 code ordinance plus a case-specific rezoning.
The ordinance polygon does not prove that ordinance created the current zoning; later cases may have changed it.
